notes.title: From Viral to Verification
notes.notes:
[p]Today, we want to tell you about something that is extremely important to us – your feedback. From the first trailer in 2023, through the development of the game, to the latest presentations at Digital Dragons 2025, it is your opinions that constantly influence the shape of Ecumene Aztec.[/p][h2]The trailer that changed everything[/h2][p]The release of the first Ecumene Aztec trailer in 2023 was a turning point for us. From a small, independent project, we became one of the most talked-about titles in the community of gamers interested in history, culture, and the action-adventure genre. It was – and still is – something wonderful![/p][p]Although the trailer went viral (60+ million views), we immediately understood the enormous expectations placed on the subject matter we were tackling. Tens of thousands of comments appeared. Some were delighted with the authenticity of the world, others rightly pointed out cultural details that could be refined, and still others pointed out that the European perspective did not fully reflect the context of the Aztec descendants.[/p][p]It was then that we began intensive collaboration with historians and ethnographers. We redesigned the protagonist, the plot, the locations and the weapons – so that Ecumene Aztec would not only be a good game, but also a culturally responsible one. It would not be a lie to say that the game has undergone a significant reboot since the first trailer in 2023. Our goal is to create a story that reflects the complexity of the conquest – not as a battle between ‘good’ and ‘evil’, but as a dramatic clash of civilisations that changed the world. In one way or another.[/p][p]Since we completely rebuilt the game, we couldn't wait for the first players to try it out... And finally, the moment arrived:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44173279/74960ff8a65a877acc45470a67493f85926f26e0.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Digital Dragons 2025 – First Live Test[/h2][p]In May 2025, we presented the playable demo of Ecumene Aztec to a wider audience for the first time. Digital Dragons in Krakow gave us the opportunity to look players in the eye – to see their reactions in real time, hear their questions and comments, and feel the emotions our game evokes...[/p][p]And we ran out of paper in our notebooks to write down everything you said...[/p][h2]What did we change?[/h2][p]Your voices are not falling on deaf ears. After Digital Dragons, we came back with a ton of notes – and immediately made specific changes:[/p][list][*][p]we improved the readability of the stealth interface – now it's easier to understand when you can perform a silent attack and what your chances of success are,[/p][/*][*][p]we adjusted the first few minutes of gameplay to better tell the story of our hero and his world,[/p][/*][*][p]We are improving the controls and responsiveness of weapons and other actions in the game so that the player always knows exactly what to do and which way to go.[/p][/*][*][p]We are improving the map of the first parts of the game to make navigation clear and understandable.[/p][/*][*][p]And that's just the tip of the iceberg, because we know that the key is testing, testing, and more testing![/p][/*][/list][h2]Feedback is important[/h2][p]It gives us energy. Your words confirm that what we are doing makes sense. When someone says, ‘I've always wanted to play a game about the Aztecs,’ we know we're on the right track. When we read, ‘Thanks to this game, I started reading about the city of Tenochtitlan,’ we feel proud.[/p][p]We recently showed you a new trailer revealing a bit of the game's plot. You already know that our hero will start as a fugitive from the sacrificial altar and will have to make decisions and become a warrior. Of course, we are closely watching your reactions. We already know that you like the Nahuatl language (the language of the Aztecs!) in the narration and are looking forward to the game because the scenario seems intriguing. We also know that we need to show you better animations of the main character. That's our priority now![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44173279/99252e3f12f5f14f341c0ed09562f3b026c3c03d.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]What's next?[/h2][p]We have more iterations ahead of us, more tests, more opportunities to listen to you. The feedback you give us is not just a ‘side note’ – it's part of our production process.[/p][p]We would like to thank everyone who played the demo, wrote a comment, gave a like, came to our stand or just smiled – because that also gives us strength.[/p][p]See you in the next post! And remember – the Aztec story lives on! Write, comment and discuss. You have a real impact on what this game will be like![/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Crafting the Story of Ecumene Aztec
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, warriors and wanderers![/h1]

As our journey into the heart of Ecumene Aztec continues, it’s time to offer a peek behind the curtain—into the world of narrative design.

[h2]Into the Fire: Research Begins[/h2]

We’re diving deep into the vibrant world of the Aztec Empire—not as ruins, but as it truly was: alive, spiritual, dangerous. Our references include the Codex Mendoza, Codex Borgia, and The True History of the Conquest of New Spain. Each is a window into another time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44173279/514329d96d3a9d18dc328a9f45d998b60027d70b.jpg[/img]

Writing a narrative in this world means more than just getting the facts straight. It means feeling the world as it once was—and making it work within a game that demands stealth, action, and survival.

[h2]A Character Transformed[/h2]
Our protagonist begins as a low-caste sacrifice. But his name, like his role, will evolve. Revenge, rebirth, and a world on fire—he walks a path from nobody to someone far more… fearsome.
We’ve detailed his backstory, look, weapon preferences—even whether he’s the type to gamble or pray. This is personal storytelling in a very impersonal world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44173279/860a80c68fe225bda3172f68586e89d7ba40fe28.jpg[/img]

[h2]What’s Next?[/h2]
The narrative backbone is almost complete. We’re finalizing the dialogue systems and planning key emotional moments… An exciting time lies ahead – the story is beginning to take an intriguing shape.
We’re working with consultants: [b]Polish writer Michał Gołkowski[/b], author of a book series set in the waning days of Aztec civilization.
Additionally, we’re collaborating with [b]Osvaldo Alexis Zúñiga Elizalde[/b], a native Nahuatl speaker who serves as our cultural consultant on Aztec heritage.

[h2]Final Thoughts[/h2]
Being a Narrative Designer means balancing history, emotion, gameplay, and myth. In Ecumene Aztec, we’re not just writing a script — we’re shaping a legend.

See you in the jungle. Or the temple. Or maybe at the altar with a fresh heart in the hand?
Do you have any questions for the Narrative Team? Feel free to ask in the comment section!
[i]— The Narrative Team @ Ecumene Games[/i]
